message.content:
Let \(z=re^{i\theta}\), where \(r>0\). Then

\[
2z+\frac1z=2re^{i\theta}+\frac1r e^{-i\theta}.
\]

Writing real and imaginary parts,

\[
2z+\frac1z=\left(2r+\frac1r\right)\cos\theta+i\left(2r-\frac1r\right)\sin\theta.
\]

Thus

\[
\left|2z+\frac1z\right|^2
=
\left(2r+\frac1r\right)^2\cos^2\theta
+
\left(2r-\frac1r\right)^2\sin^2\theta.
\]

Expanding,

\[
\left|2z+\frac1z\right|^2
=
4r^2+\frac1{r^2}+4(\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta).
\]

Since \(\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta=1-2\sin^2\theta\), the condition becomes

\[
4r^2+\frac1{r^2}+4(1-2\sin^2\theta)=1.
\]

So

\[
4r^2+\frac1{r^2}=8\sin^2\theta-3.
\]

By AM-GM,

\[
4r^2+\frac1{r^2}\ge 2\sqrt{4r^2\cdot \frac1{r^2}}=4.
\]

Hence

\[
8\sin^2\theta-3\ge 4,
\]

so

\[
\sin^2\theta\ge \frac78.
\]

Equality occurs when \(r^2=\frac12\), which is allowed, so the minimum is attainable.

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac78}\).
